## As asked

<!-- harbour-periodical-gate id="security-review" -->
Operator note: Tail Periodical for the LIN-4395 autopilot run (oldest due repo lane)

**Repository:** `JKershaw/LinearViewer` (Harbour). **Remit:** `generateSecurityReviewPrompt` in `lib/periodicals.js` (registry entry `id: 'security-review'`). **Mode:** review only. The deliverable is one committed report plus the area-note edits it calls for, in **one docs-only PR**. This run files **no follow-up tickets**.

**Last report:** `docs/reviews/security-review-2026-10-23.md` (LIN-3776). It measured `c6c5585a`. The earlier reports are `security-review-2026-10-18.md` and `security-review-2026-06-25.md` in the same folder. At seeding (`origin/main` `008d38bb`, 10 Nov), HEAD was **470 commits** past `c6c5585a`. Re-ground everything at the HEAD you actually run on.

**Where the report goes:** `docs/reviews/security-review-<run date>.md`, the series convention. Bulky evidence, if you need any, goes in `docs/reviews/_evidence-<date>/`. Do not invent another location.

## 0. Audit the scope before you execute it

Treat the scope below as a starting point to **extend**, not a checklist to stay inside. Before you review anything, look for surfaces that are in remit but not listed here, and fold them in: new routes, pages, token types, outbound calls, grants and operator scripts. If all you could do with this scope is shrink it, be suspicious of that. The expected move is to widen it to everything the remit reaches.

Widen **what you examine**, not **what you report**. The report stays uncapped and severity-ranked, and a near-empty result is a genuine outcome. What you write stays bounded: a note entry only where a finding binds a builder or leaves work waiting in an area, and every note stays under its cap.

**Sibling seams.** A surface no single review owns is in this one's scope. The sibling reviews are listed in `lib/periodicals.js`; read their latest reports for where their remits stop.

* **Dependency & Supply-Chain** (`docs/reviews/dependency-supply-chain-review-2026-10-23.md`) owns CVE triage (LIN-620). This review still owns the vendored `public/*.min.js` (DOMPurify, marked, Chart.js), which sit outside `package.json`.
* **Stability** (`stability-review-2026-11-08.md`) and **Integration & Surface Maturity** (`integration-surface-maturity-review-2026-11-10.md`) own availability. This review owns the abuse half of any rate limit or ceiling.
* **The runner contract with** `JKershaw/simple-dispatcher` straddles two repos. The last run put the Harbour side in remit (`routes/proxy-runner.js`, `lib/runner-kit/*`, grants, runner prompt) and read the SD broker only as contract input. Re-decide this explicitly and record the decision. Since then, SD's `harbour-token-mcp-server.js` (the credential-injecting broker behind `HARBOUR_LOCAL_BASE`) changed under LIN-4378. It holds the bootstrap in its own process env, and it runs as the same OS user as the agent, the same boundary as LIN-3778.

## 1. Read prior runs first

Read `docs/reviews/security-review-2026-10-23.md` in full: its severity table, its fix-claim table, its "Not verified" list and its Adversarial Second-Read section. Build on it as a **delta**. Don't re-derive it, and don't re-flag what is handled. Ticket states below are as of 10 Nov; re-check each one.

**Closed since the last run. Verify each as an attacker would test it, with a cheap mutation check where possible:**

* LIN-3780 / LIN-3794 / LIN-3795 / LIN-3796 / LIN-3818: secret-scan coverage for the incident types, ATCTT3, prefixed Harbour tokens (`9aa68bb8`), and PEMs split or truncated on `/t/` pages. Does the scanner still miss anything the incident or Harbour itself mints? LIN-2853 is still open.
* LIN-2852 (`7d8953a1`, source scan fails closed) and LIN-2851 (`e7d75987`, tracked `.env` and `data/` scanned). LIN-2850 is still open.
* LIN-619 (`b4c7bb97`): production refuses to boot without a real `SESSION_SECRET`.
* LIN-3779: Flight Companion `remember` on auto-wake and boot turns.
* LIN-3772: least-privileged Mongo user. Does the `lin3014_read` question (2026-10-23 N5) close with it?
* LIN-3789 (`c93f8792`) removed the global email send ceiling that the last second read ranked first (#11), and kept a volume alarm. Confirm the per-address and per-IP limits now carry abuse resistance on their own, and that the per-IP key is safe under `trust proxy`.
* LIN-3699 (401 versus retryable 503 on token auth), LIN-3346 (one public-path exemption for PAT auto-login), LIN-3875 / LIN-3856 (precompute now behind the free-tier gate: does that close LIN-3422's D4?).
* LIN-4378 (`f7d1923e`): the rate limit is keyed per proven credential, and `proxyLimiter` runs before auth by design. Can an unauthenticated caller rotate keys to escape it, or exhaust another credential's bucket?
* LIN-3849 / LIN-3643 / LIN-1374: re-read only what the 2026-10-23 rows routed to them.

**Still open. Re-verify; don't re-file:** LIN-3386 (forged authority marks, the top High last time), LIN-3394, LIN-1410, LIN-3778, LIN-684, LIN-737, LIN-676, LIN-3402, LIN-3417, LIN-3422, LIN-3425, LIN-3273, LIN-3281, LIN-2850, LIN-2853, LIN-2530, LIN-2642, LIN-1912, LIN-3593, LIN-3770, LIN-3836, and **LIN-4215** (any workspace member can mint read and read-write proxy tokens since LIN-3849; filed after the last run and never assessed by this series).

**Never reached in depth last time:** the roadmap, `collective-participant` and `ship-biscuit-editor` prompt builders; the "Not verified" production items, to be recorded again if still unreachable.

## 2. New surface since `c6c5585a` (seed list; extend it)

* **New proxy routes:** `POST /api/proxy/periodicals/:id/mint` (dispatch grant, LIN-4313/4317), which renders an operator `note` into a minted agent's prompt. That makes it an injection sink for whoever holds `dispatch`. Also `/api/proxy/model-routing/*` reads and writes, `POST /api/proxy/runner/usage/:id` (LIN-4198, the take grant), and `POST /api/proxy/issues/:id/description/below`.
* **New session-lane routes:** `POST /api/dispatch/usage/:itemId` (dispatch-token auth, `feedbackLimiter`); settings model routing and presets; `effort-readout`, `escalation-kpis`, `observation`, `live-console`, `passage-planner`; dashboard `hydrate/:wsUrlKey/:identifier`, which takes a second urlKey in the path, so check tenant isolation; session-context, run and session summaries; `collective/preview`; `POST /auth/openrouter/consent/clear`; public `/getting-started(.md)`.
* **Agent-written repo content:** Periodicals and the builder's leftover step now write `docs/areas/*.md` on main (LIN-4347, LIN-4371, LIN-4379), and every later prompt reads those notes as grounding (`GROUNDING_BY_KIND` in `lib/prompt-formatters.js`). Trace whether externally-influenceable text can reach a note, and so persist as instruction into later runs. The guard is `tests/unit/area-notes.test.js`.
* **The As-asked block and the size record** (LIN-4362, LIN-4369): server-side immutability of the filed words. Is this a technical boundary or prose?
* **Whole-life cost reads and the session timeline** (LIN-4404, LIN-4405, LIN-4263): cross-workspace reads within a lineage.

## 3. Run the review, grounded in real handlers at HEAD

**a. Exposed credentials.** Scan the git-tracked tree **and** its full history, using built-in `git` only (`git grep` over the tree, `git log -p` / `-G` over history including `--all`). Introduce no scanner dependency. Derive the patterns at run time:

* the `lib/secret-scan.js` set;
* Harbour's own minted-token prefixes (LIN-3795);
* Linear, GitHub, OpenRouter, Atlassian, Resend and Mongo URI formats;
* PEM headers;
* generic `KEY=` / `SECRET=` / `PASSWORD=` / `TOKEN=` assignments;
* the known cloud-provider prefixes.

Trap: a HEAD-only scan misses a live secret in a past commit. A confirmed live secret is neutralised only by removing it from tracked content **and** rotating it at source. Flag any history rewrite as a human decision. Never suppress, allowlist or delete from the tree only. Never copy a secret value anywhere.

**b. Injection and trust boundaries.** Trace untrusted input to the sinks where it crosses into a trusted channel:

* the inputs: request bodies, query params, tracker titles, descriptions and comments (any GitHub account on a public-repo workspace), PR check names, operator notes;
* the sinks: shell (`lib/harbour-spawn.js`, `lib/bash-tool.js`), Mongo queries, HTML output (`lib/render*.js`), and every prompt assembled for an AI worker.

Flag where one path carries input as **data** while a parallel path interpolates it as code. An instruction telling a model to behave is an aspirational guard, not a technical boundary.

**c. The broad classes:**

* broken access control and workspace isolation (session lane and proxy lane);
* authentication and sessions (OAuth `state`, email sign-in, cookie and session lifetime);
* sensitive-data exposure (public `/t/` and `/kpis`, logs, transcripts);
* SSRF and outbound requests;
* misconfiguration (CSP, HSTS, the `req.hostname` 301, `trust proxy`);
* dependency risk at the seam named above.

These classes are a **floor, not a ceiling**. Discover the complete set for this remit from the repo.

Severity-rank by blast radius. A vector reaching command execution, a merge, an enqueue, or cross-tenant data outranks a low-scope, mitigated or theoretical one.

## 4. Write an uncapped report

Write the report to `docs/reviews/security-review-<date>.md`. Use the 2026-10-23 shape: verdict, severity table with a delta column, fix-claim table, classes and how each was bounded, credentials, "Not verified", and a second-read appendix. Ground each finding against source at HEAD, not prior prose. Don't pad it.

## 5. Feed the area notes, and file no follow-up tickets

Read `docs/areas/README.md` and follow its rules, not any assumed here: the registry `docs/areas/areas.json` (first match wins), the note format (`## Lessons` / `## Waiting`), the guard `tests/unit/area-notes.test.js` and the **6144-byte cap**, plus `LEFTOVER_RULE` in `lib/prompts/leftover-words.js`.

**Start from what landed.** List the files changed in `c6c5585a..HEAD` and map each to its area. At seeding the counts were:

| Area | Changed files |
| -- | -- |
| runs-and-dispatch | 81 |
| front-end-pages | 74 |
| front-end-browser | 73 |
| llm-and-prompts | 56 |
| web-routes | 37 |
| auth-accounts-and-workspaces | 33 |
| agent-api | 27 |
| other-features | 21 |
| providers | 11 |
| platform-and-plumbing | 7 |
| reports-and-operator-tools | 6 |
| task-model | 2 |
| wiring | 1 |

`llm-and-prompts.md` (6139 B) and `runs-and-dispatch.md` (6140 B) are already **at the cap**. Any entry you add there means pruning or distilling first.

**How to write entries:**

* In each note you touch, prune entries that are settled or no longer true.
* A finding that leaves work in an area gets a **Waiting** entry. A rule a builder there must follow gets a **Lesson**.
* Each entry cites the area's file first, then names its source as "(Security Review, <run date>)" with this report as the second cited path.
* A finding already filed as a ticket (every open ticket above) stays in the report only, never also in a note.

**Route each finding that has no area note to the person, never to a ticket:**

* **A larger tidy:** write a Waiting entry worded as a size of move, and list it in the closing comment.
* **No area file to cite** (lockfiles, vendored libraries, a live secret, ops facts): put it in the closing comment, addressed to the person.
* **A cross-area seam:** file it under the area a change would start from, naming the other side, and say in the report that seams have no full home in the notes yet.

**The PR.** Commit the report and the note edits together in one docs-only PR, then rebase it onto `main`. Get it green: `ci-success` (unit, the E2E shards and the secret scan) with the notes guard passing.

## 6. Stay review-only

* Change no code, config, tests or secrets, and no docs beyond the report and the area-note edits.
* Never copy a real secret value into the report, this task or a branch.
* An instruction to avoid touching files covers the code under review, not this deliverable.

## 7. Adversarial second read (required, before hand-off)

After the report and note edits are written, a genuinely separate reader answers cold: *"What is the largest item in this window that this report missed or misfiled?"*

* **Tier 1** (preferred): a wholly separate session.
* **Tier 2** (accepted): a fresh-context sub-agent with no memory of the report-writing turn.
* **Tier 3** (not accepted): this session re-reading its own report.

State which tier you used. Post **one** comment on this task containing all three lines together:

* `Adversarial second-read verdict: AGREE` or `Adversarial second-read verdict: DISAGREE`
* `Differed from top finding: YES` or `Differed from top finding: NO`
* `Disposition: fixed in place`, `Disposition: escalated`, or `Disposition: no change`

Copy the same three fields into a `## Adversarial Second-Read` section of the report, with the tier, the question and the reader's full answer. A DISAGREE verdict is itself the escalation. It never holds back the hand-off.

## 8. Hand off. Don't stop silently, and don't merge or set Done

1. As soon as the PR is open, post its full URL as a comment on this task.
2. Post the second-read comment from §7.
3. Post a closing comment: a concise, severity-ranked summary with the report path and the PR. It lists for the person any larger tidy and any finding with no area file to cite. It names who finishes: **review approves, then close-out merges the PR, sets this task to Done and posts the final summary.**

This run neither merges nor moves the task to Done, so the task stays In Progress until close-out. If the PR cannot be made green, name the blocker in the closing comment instead.

*End of what was asked. Steps write below this line; nothing above it changes.*

## Size of the move

**Size:** just the task
**Why:** One severity-ranked security delta report with its area-note entries in one docs-only pull request; neither a Survey nor any area note shows something this review needs before it can be run and reported.
**Cuts:** none
**Decided by:** the standing policy

## Outcome

Implemented and merged on 10 Nov 2026:

* **PR:** [https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2394](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2394>), merged as `da5df707`.
* **Deployed:** Harbour / production `success` at 15:13 UTC.
* **Content:** `docs/reviews/security-review-2026-11-10.md`, which measured `4d23fa15` (474 commits past `c6c5585a`), plus six area-note edits (`agent-api`, `auth-accounts-and-workspaces`, `front-end-pages`, `llm-and-prompts`, `platform-and-plumbing`, `web-routes`). No tickets were filed.
* **Close-out fixes from review:** one commit, `58750173`.
  * F1: the second reader's answer, restored verbatim.
  * F2: the session-lifetime row added to the classes table.
  * F3: the row-22 typo fixed.

**Deviation from the plan:** a Tier 2 second read surfaced the SD broker's unauthenticated loopback listener. It was added as a conditional High at row 2, and the verdict was qualified to "either Harbour lane".

The research findings, the full plan and the stage history are preserved in the task snapshots and the comment trail. The person-facing hand-off is in the `## Close-out — LIN-4411` comment.

## Implementation Plan

Implemented as approved, apart from the second-read deviation above. fits one session.
